I've been doing this wheat-maize rotation on these 10.1 mu for 30 years now. With the kids grown and my husband taking outside work, I manage most of the field work myself and hire help only at harvest. Let me think through this year carefully.

For my winter wheat, I'll stick with an improved variety like Jimai 22 — it's given me around 520 kg/mu consistently and resists lodging. I plant around October 10. Before sowing I'll do one rotary tillage to mix in the maize stubble. For base fertilizer I apply one bag of diammonium phosphate (50 kg, giving me about 9 kg P₂O₅ and 1.8 kg N per mu) plus 15 kg of potassium sulfate (~7.5 kg K₂O per mu). Then at jointing in early March I topdress 25 kg of urea per mu (~11.5 kg N). That brings my total N to roughly 20 kg/mu. I know the extension people say 16–18 is enough, but I'd rather put on a little extra urea than watch a yellow field in April. Urea is only about 2.4 yuan/kg — losing 50 kg of grain costs me far more.

Irrigation: I'll water 4 times from the well — once before winter to protect against freeze, then at jointing, heading, and grain-filling. Pesticide: one herbicide spray in spring for broadleaf weeds, one combined spray at heading for aphids and powdery mildew, plus a "one-spray-three-prevention" at grain fill. Three sprays total.

For summer maize after wheat harvest in mid-June, I'll direct-seed a hybrid — Zhengdan 958 or Denghai 605, both reliable here. No-tillage, just seed straight into the wheat stubble. I use a compound fertilizer (15-15-15) at sowing, 40 kg/mu, then side-dress 20 kg urea at the big-trumpet stage. That's about 15 kg N, 6 kg P₂O₅, 6 kg K₂O per mu. Maize usually gets enough summer rain here, but in a dry July I'll irrigate once. For pests I spray once for corn borer and armyworm around the big-trumpet stage, and usually a second spray if aphids build up. I expect around 580 kg/mu — last three years averaged that.

My total fertilizer budget runs about 350 yuan per mu across both crops, pesticides another 80 yuan, seed 60 yuan, irrigation electricity 70 yuan. With machinery services for harvest and sowing, roughly 800 yuan/mu in cash costs. At current grain prices I should net around 700–800 yuan/mu across the two crops. That's my plan.
